name: Bran Granite Bough
loreTies: The living world adapts and endures.
Living Grove: terrain and sustain effects grow stronger over time.
Bran Granite Bough is a colossal Tuatha deity shaped by the living world adapts and endures. It manifests the Realm's law through battlefield-scale mythic force.
shortBackstory: Morrígan, Battle-Crow Fate Queen, is one of the four playable deities of the Tuatha canon. The lore remains the same; the playable form is now the source-realm divinity behind the mythology: war fate goddess, battle-crow prophecy, sovereignty terror and doom rupture.

chapters.title: Origin
chapters.text: Bran Granite Bough began as more than a weapon in Avalora. Bran Granite Bough was bound to a living grove scar in Avalora during a Gate disturbance that tested whether the living world adapts and endures could survive contact with the Hollow. The title carried in their name was earned when the Titan chose duty over spectacle and accepted a burden ordinary soldiers could not survive.

chapters.title: Faction Bond
chapters.text: Among the Tuatha, Bran Granite Bough is treated as proof that an ancient civilization intertwined with sacred forests, fae danger, living stones, druidic force, and moonlit grove law can become battlefield doctrine without losing its soul. Their silhouette carries emerald, silver, living wood, ancient stones, roots, bark-bronze skin, antler crowns, moonlit grove power, but their real identity is tactical: adaptation, healing, roots, terrain control, endurance through life systems. Every deployment makes faction philosophy visible through movement, restraint, and force.

chapters.title: Gate Wound
chapters.text: The Gate did not simply attack Bran Granite Bough; it tried to measure what their Realm values most. The wound echoed sacred doctrine back as bait, tempting the Titan to overextend, break battle line, or turn culture into raw fuel. Bran Granite Bough survived by refusing the Gate's terms, leaving a scar that still reacts whenever adaptive roots appears on the map.

chapters.title: Campaign Role
chapters.text: In The First Reopening, Bran Granite Bough gives the campaign a personal lens on faction survival. Their presence reinforces the rule that faction identity stays distinct unless a mission explicitly permits otherwise. In a one-active-deity Titan, Bran Granite Bough turns Living Grove from a passive rule into a story statement: the Realm is defending its meaning.

chapters.title: Personal Conflict
chapters.text: Bran Granite Bough's flaw is overcommitment to the belief that their Realm's answer must always be enough. NPC witnesses and rival factions challenge that certainty as the Hollow learns to imitate law, oath, balance, life, radiance, and ambition without understanding any of them. Their battlefield stats support this arc: HP 32, attack 7, range 2, speed 2, energy 3.

relationshipHooks: Cross-faction envoys can challenge their doctrine without erasing their faction identity.

visualCanon: Maeve is Avalora’s root-memory voice. Her silver-branch regalia, thorn records, moss-veiled cloak, crow omen marks, and calm dangerous beauty should feel like the origin behind later fae queens and druid archives.
